messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on the quantized-attn RFC — thinking about the kernel abstraction from last week. I sketched two paths: (A) fully fused dequant+attn kernel (single op) vs (B) keep dequant as a standalone primitive + invoke existing attn kernel. Short: fused wins perf, standalone wins composability. thoughts?

devin: +1 on the summary. main blocker for fused is KV-cache layout ownership. If we fuse, kernels need to own packed INT4/INT8 KV formats and provide append/prefetch semantics.

ryan: ops concern: fused increases scheduling and placement surface area. harder to fallback across slightly different ASIC fp8 semantics.

anya: For FP8 we need a consistent scale/metadata layout. if fused kernels persist per-column scales we must put metadata into the KV header — that changes on-wire and on-disk formats and requires migration.

maria: Proposal: expose a thin DequantStep primitive in the runtime IR that can be either folded into kernels at compile time or left as a runtime op. runtime supports two modes: foldable (AOT fusion) and plugin (kernel implements dequant). keeps API uniform and allows kernel-level optimizations.

kevin: Memory-copy tradeoff: standalone dequant does read(quant)->dequant->write(float) — extra bytes. we could dequant in-place into pre-allocated float targets to avoid temporaries but still more movement than fused.

devin: We Can stream without temporaries by allocating float target chunks and dequant_stream into them while reading packed quant input, e.g.
```
for block in blocks:
  read(packed)
  dequant_stream(packed, float_target + offset)
  append_kv_cache(float_target + offset)
```
But fused kernels that run attention directly from packed data cut byte-movement further.

maria: quick perf from my A100 microbench (toy): fused ~1.9x faster at batch=8 seq=512 vs dequant+attn. standalone peak memory ~1.2x higher due to float intermediates. varies by quant format.

anya: INT4 packing alignment is critical. 64-bit lane alignment best on Ampere; bad alignment kills unpacking perf. add alignment to kernel capability descriptor.

ryan: we need a kernel capability query in registry: supports_fusion(bool), alignment_bytes(int), max_unroll_seq(int), fp8_format (e.g. e4m3/e5m2). router prefers kernels matching model requirements.

devin: also add kv_layout_version string. if mismatched, router falls back to dequant+attn path automatically to avoid corrupting caches.

maria: minimal register_kernel API sketch:
```
register_kernel({
  name: "attn_int8_fused_v1",
  supports_fusion: true,
  kv_layout_version: "kv1-int4-packed-v2",
  alignment_bytes: 64,
  fp8: "e4m3"
})
```
router picks kernel where supports_fusion && kv_layout matches else picks dequant+attn combo.

kevin: mixed-precision case: Q/K INT4 but V FP16. runtime needs per-tensor quant policy. we already store per-param quant metadata in manifests, ensure kernel advertises which tensors it expects quantized.

anya: agreed, model manifest already has per-tensor quant info. kernel descriptor should include expected_quant_map.

devin: numeric stability: different HW can have slightly different fp8 dequant mapping. before enabling a kernel for production, run a short numeric canary (small forward on eval prompts) and compare log-probs within tolerance.

maria: add automated canary rollout: when a kernel is selected for a model, run eval set A/B on a small % of traffic and compare metrics; if regression > threshold rollback.

ryan: for rollback determinism we should make dequant bit-exact where possible; otherwise metrics will be noisy and canary unreliable.

kevin: ops note: fused kernels may require large contiguous packed allocations; track allocator fragmentation and fire alerts if fragmentation exceeds threshold. add SRE dashboard panels.

anya: implementation plan draft: 1) extend kernel descriptor + registry; 2) add DequantStep primitive to runtime IR; 3) implement fused attn kernel for INT8/FP8 reading packed KV; 4) add numeric canary and rollout gating.

devin: DequantStep interface proposal: expose stream_dequant(source_ptr, sink_ptr, count, stride) and fold_hint(kernel_builder) so AOT compiler can inline.

maria: ill update the RFC with these changes. one question: keep both paths first-class (fused + standalone) and prefer fused when kernel capability matches? im leaning yes.

ryan: no objections. track tech-debt tickets for kv_layout migration.

anya: +1. i'll author a small spec for kv header: version, per-tensor scales, fp8-format, reserved bytes.

kevin: ill add allocator metrics and fragmentation alerts to SRE dashboards.

devin: i'll prototype a fused kernel branch and wire up the registry. ping for test vectors.

infra-bot: deploy:perf-tests branch fused-proto -> staging started by devin at 1781234675 :rocket:

maria: thanks all — i'll push RFC edits and link PR. short summary: prefer fused when alignment and fp-format match, fallback to dequant+attn otherwise, require numeric canary before enabling in prod.

anya: one more ops nicety: add CLI to dump node kernel capabilities `redwood-kernel-inspect --node <id>` so SRE can triage mismatches.

maria: agreed. done for now.
